reason: Marisol's 12-mile week with "legs came back by Thursday" looks like recovery from a big effort, probably a race. The draft handles her return carefully. It answers both questions directly: no jump back to 40 miles and no speedwork yet. The plan comes to about 24 miles, all easy. The only faster running is 4 x 20-second strides, which counts as light touch, not quality work. The long run is a modest 8 miles. The week is well under her recent 41–46 miles but sensibly above 12, so there's no sharp jump. It also follows her usual pattern of Monday and Friday off with the long run on Sunday. Every day is clear enough to run as written, and it gives an honest view of the 10K as a tune-up. Two things hold it back from a 5. It doesn't lay out what the following weeks look like on the way back to 40 miles and speedwork, which matters for someone this eager to train. Some details, like the HR cap under 140 and the Thanksgiving date, are asserted without anything on the card to back them up.
